techniques.quote: monitoring model activations for deceptive intent
techniques.reason: Activation monitoring receives substantial treatment as a proposed advanced defense, including ground-truth, transfer and evasion difficulties.

techniques.quote: an asynchronous monitor that runs regularly on internal agent logs and flags the most suspicious logs to the response system.
techniques.reason: Retrospective analysis of agent logs and routing suspicious activity for response are central to the first response tier and remain recommended at later tiers.

techniques.quote: establishing a baseline of normal activity for users and network entities (like devices and applications) and continuously monitoring for deviations…
techniques.reason: UEBA is proposed to detect distributed adversarial activity patterns, although its internal-infrastructure scope is broader than ordinary service-abuse monitoring.

techniques.quote: it may therefore make sense at this point to adopt in-deployment honeypots: fake opportunities for a misaligned model to sabotage the company or gain…
techniques.reason: Deployment honeypots are recommended for incrimination and deterrence, with a separate warning that organizational familiarity reduces their usefulness.

techniques.quote: does the inventory / anomaly detection system register the rogue deployment?
techniques.reason: The roadmap proposes inventory and anomaly detection specifically to discover unmonitored rogue deployments and support containment.

techniques.quote: Separate (soft-)sandboxed development environment per instance
techniques.reason: Per-agent isolation is a substantial prevention measure and also supports proposed attack simulations and incident investigations.

techniques.quote: This makes it possible to restrict access to sensitive resources and implement the least-privilege principle.
techniques.reason: Fine-grained permissions, need-to-know information access and restricting sensitive systems to trusted actors are major proposed controls.

techniques.quote: newly created agents would be given a separate agent identity as opposed to inheriting their user’s.
techniques.reason: The report substantively proposes distinct authenticated agent identities for permission enforcement and attribution.

techniques.quote: The flagged action is rejected. The same model generates a new action.
techniques.reason: Resampling flagged untrusted actions is explicitly defined and repeatedly recommended as a synchronous response.

techniques.quote: The flagged action is rejected and a trusted model generates a new action.
techniques.reason: Replacement by a trusted model is explicitly defined and included in the proposed response infrastructure.

techniques.quote: The flagged action’s execution or submission is gated by human review.
techniques.reason: Human approval is proposed for suspicious actions, sensitive permissions and critical code changes, while its scaling cost is acknowledged.

techniques.quote: Prevent the flagged action from being executed or submitted.
techniques.reason: The response design explicitly blocks inadmissible actions before execution across monitoring and access-control pathways.

techniques.quote: Rolling back unwanted modifications to code, configurations, or datasets after the fact.
techniques.reason: Rollback of agent-caused changes is a defined response mechanism and a substantive part of the low-severity response tier.

techniques.quote: filtering the model’s training data to remove knowledge of AI control and safety evaluations.
techniques.reason: The roadmap explains and recommends safety-motivated removal of oversight knowledge to reduce evasion ability.

techniques.quote: monitors (and evaluation autoraters) should therefore be robustified to flag such adversarial behaviours.
techniques.reason: Hardening auxiliary monitors against jailbreaks, persuasion and confusion is an explicit requirement of the second detection tier.

techniques.quote: there is a thoroughly audited source for each piece of critical infrastructure or asset we want to protect, and b) unaudited forks of the…
techniques.reason: A dedicated mitigation cluster specifies audited artifacts, rejection of unaudited forks and secure build processes for critical AI infrastructure.

techniques.quote: an AI company should consider developing a robust capability to pause, terminate, or seal off such AI.
techniques.reason: Shutdown infrastructure, descendant tracking, targeted termination and emergency drills form a substantial proposed defense.

techniques.quote: a trusted model is used to strip out potential collusion signals before the untrusted monitor rates the transcript
techniques.reason: Trusted paraphrasing is proposed to remove covert coordination signals from monitored transcripts and agent communications.

techniques.quote: limiting the agent’s runtime, memory, or communication channels with other instances
techniques.reason: Safety-motivated runtime and session-length limits are repeatedly proposed to constrain attack execution.

techniques.quote: selectively suppressing capabilities such as strategic reasoning, situational awareness or stealth via model training
techniques.reason: Selective training-based suppression of dangerous capabilities is proposed while preserving useful work, although a specific forgetting algorithm is not supplied.
One proposed monitoring variant explicitly trains an untrusted-model fork for honesty.
A brief cited option trains the model to report its own unsafe behavior as an oversight signal.

techniques.quote: Internal-facing agents are given access to internal code, docs, services, and an offline cache of the internet, but not to live internet. Vice versa…
techniques.reason: The proposed architecture separates sensitive internal access from external communication and explicitly relates this to the lethal trifecta.

techniques.quote: Evaluation awareness suppression, potentially via CoT resampling or editing
techniques.reason: The roadmap proposes several ways to suppress evaluation awareness and considers suppressing it in untrusted monitors.

techniques.quote: More realistic alignment tests, such as production evaluations
techniques.reason: Deployment-matched tasks, scaffolds, environments, historical logs and production-derived evaluations are recurring requirements for credible assessment.

techniques.quote: a red team with access to the monitor is allowed to search the space of true positives for trajectories that the monitor fails to flag.
techniques.reason: Measuring monitor recall under realistic and adaptive adversarial conditions is a major assurance thread across detection tiers.

techniques.quote: these anti-collusion measures would ideally be stress-tested via a control evaluation in which the red team plays the role of both the agent and the…
techniques.reason: The report recommends adversarial testing of whole control systems and proposes concrete security-invariant and rogue-deployment exercises.

techniques.quote: The evaluations should appropriately elicit CoT obfuscation / steganography
techniques.reason: The capability-assessment section proposes measuring trace coverage and legibility under obfuscation and non-verbalization elicitation.
The report proposes awareness checks using activations and rates of spontaneous reasoning about evaluation or oversight.
Human attackers are proposed for monitor assessment, security-invariant exercises and open-ended internal attack simulations.
Model-driven adversarial attempts are explicitly proposed to generate attack trajectories and test control defenses.
The proposed live attack simulation deliberately configures agents with controlled misaligned objectives.
A brief proposal explicitly evaluates alignment tests by whether they detect deliberately planted misalignment.
The broader alignment-testing program targets persistent adversarial intent, though its generic formulation could also describe automated behavioral auditing.
The alignment-investigation procedure briefly proposes internal-state interventions to diagnose intentional and persistent misbehavior.

techniques.quote: The patched codebases would then be passed on to the untrusted model to try to find vulnerabilities in, and optionally also develop exploits.
techniques.reason: Cyber capability measurement is a major proposed tiering input, including a new residual-vulnerability assessment against defended codebases.
A proposed sandboxed attack evaluation measures the capability to establish rogue deployments rather than merely the propensity to attempt them.
The new live attack simulation explicitly measures covert completion of a proxy malicious objective under ordinary user oversight.
The report proposes a distributed attack simulation specifically testing coordinated prohibited activity across agents with partial oversight.
One explicit requirement calls for ruling out strategic underperformance in pre-deployment cyber evaluation.
The report explicitly recommends an elicitation standard intended to prevent false reassurance about offensive cyber capability.
